prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse near-to-far layout: walls, mirrors, and hanging clothes are mostly several metres away, while the clothing rack entering the lower foreground in frames 1–3 appears within roughly 0.3–1 m of the camera wearer. The detected people near the mirrors in frames 1–4 appear roughly 2–4 m away, whereas the large person in frame 5 is approximately 0.5–1.5 m in front and slightly right of the wearer; the far-right figure or reflection is roughly 2–4 m away and partly outside the view. Across frames 1–3 the camera moves or turns past the nearby rack, producing increasing foreground occlusion, and by frame 5 the closest person occupies much more of the view, consistent with approach or a turn toward them. Depth makes foreground clearance and distance ordering clearer than RGB, but estimates around mirrors, the bright window, motion-blurred frame 3, and object boundaries are unreliable, and reflected people may receive physically incorrect depths.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates several person-shaped regions from the dark background: two small, closely spaced people or reflections appear left of centre in frames 1 and 2, multiple overlapping person regions appear near the centre in frame 3, one small person appears near the middle-left of frame 4, and a much larger person fills the centre-right of frame 5. In the early frames the paired regions are roughly 0.2–0.6 m apart in the image plane and about 2–4 m from the wearer, while the frame-5 person is much nearer, roughly 0.5–1.5 m away and within possible arm's reach; another person is clipped at the extreme right and is farther away or reflected. The masks reveal distinct people despite blur and overlap, and show partial occlusions in frame 3 and truncation at the right edge in frame 5, but they provide little direct depth, facing direction, or information about unlabelled racks, walls, and clothing. The frame-3 region labelled "umbrella" does not match the RGB scene clearly, some person masks may correspond to mirror reflections, and several masks merge, fragment, or omit body parts, so object identity and physical separation are uncertain.
descriptions.pose: The pose map supports body orientation and articulation: upright yellow skeletons in frames 1, 2, and 4 are approximately 2–4 m ahead and slightly left or near centre, while frame 3 contains overlapping, distorted skeletons near the centre and frame 5 shows a much larger upper-body/hand configuration close to the camera. The early upright figures appear mostly side-on or oblique rather than squarely facing the wearer; in frame 5 the shoulders and magenta hands are oriented toward the camera region, although head and eye direction are not reliable enough to confirm gaze. The frame-5 hands lie in front of the person's torso and appear within that person's arm's reach, while the person as a whole is roughly 0.5–1.5 m from the wearer and may also be within the wearer's arm's reach; the smaller earlier figures are not. Pose makes limb arrangement, facing changes, and close hand location clearer than RGB, but missing keypoints, implausible long connections in frames 3 and 5, overlap, mirror reflections, motion blur, and bodies partly outside the frame make exact orientation, distance, and occlusion relationships unreliable.
